cases.summary: The general manager of Costa Rica's central bank, Hazel Valverde, filed a criminal complaint against Rocío Aguilar, the superintendent general of financial entities, after she refused to hand the central bank data on credit operations that included borrowers' identity numbers. The complaint was first for disobeying authority; after a raid the prosecution service reclassified it as breach of official duty, influence-peddling and influence against the public treasury. Aguilar disclosed on 17 August 2023 that she had been reported, and on 1 September 2023 the anti-corruption prosecution unit searched the records office of the financial system council, Conassif, inside the central bank's own headquarters. The case file is 23-000107-1218-PE and Aguilar was the only person charged; investigators were also examining whether Conassif members bore any responsibility. The data protection agency ordered the central bank to suspend requests for information containing personal data while its own case was decided, and the president of Conassif called the complaint baseless.
cases.source_title: Los rostros, las claves y lo que se sabe hasta ahora del caso del Banco Central contra la superintendente Rocío Aguilar

cases.category: audit finding on dormant state accounts held at the central bank
cases.people: Deodat Sharma (Auditor General of Guyana)
cases.summary: Guyana's Auditor General, Deodat Sharma, reported in his 2013 report that eight accounts at the Bank of Guyana holding about 1.8 billion Guyana dollars had sat unused for more than five years, untouched since 2009. The individual balances he listed were 474 million for UK Programme Aid-GEA, 371 million for the Infrastructural Development Fund, 280 million for the Agriculture Rehabilitation Project, 213 million for SIMAP Phase II, 172 million for the Financial Sector Reform Programme, 127 million for Accountant General-GEC Wartsila, 77 million for an Agriculture Loan and 55 million for UK Programme Aid-Rice. The Audit Office had reviewed eleven special accounts at the Bank of Guyana with balances of about 4.3 billion dollars in total. The Auditor General said the money belonged in the Consolidated Fund and recommended the Ministry of Finance transfer it there as soon as possible, noting that on that basis the government's overall bank position would show a positive balance of 56 billion dollars.
cases.source_title: AG discovers $1.8B in eight unused BoG accounts

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
cases.category: questioned procurement at a central bank subsidiary
cases.people: Central Engraving and Printing Plant (the central bank's banknote printing works); two anonymous domestic card makers who raised the complaints
cases.summary: A September 2019 Mirror Media investigation questioned how the Central Engraving and Printing Plant, which the article describes as being under Taiwan's central bank, came to hold the contract to produce the country's new digital national identity cards. The plan was announced by Premier Su Tseng-chang on 22 August with the plant in charge and about NT$4 billion budgeted, and an open tender had been planned for October 2019. On 14 June 2019 the tender was switched to a restricted tender, which the article says was not publicly justified, and the budget reportedly rose to about NT$4.8 billion. A subcontract tender issued by Bank of Taiwan on 26 August for chip cards and printing equipment required bidders to show more than NT$1.2 billion in sales experience, which the article says no domestic firm could meet. Two anonymous domestic card makers argued the plant had no chip-card experience and that the rules favoured foreign suppliers. The article notes the plant had previously printed about 550,000 passports with a wrong airport photograph inside, at a cost to the treasury of about NT$220 million; the plant said it was only the contractor and did not lead that project. The article alleges no bribery and reports no criminal investigation, charges or court outcome.
cases.source_title: Mirror Media investigation into the Central Engraving and Printing Plant's digital ID card contract (2 September 2019)

cases.people: Pierre Laporte (former governor)
cases.summary: Pierre Laporte, who left the governorship of the Central Bank of Seychelles in March 2012 to become finance minister, was accused in an anonymous letter circulated in September 2012 of drawing two salaries at the same time, one from the central bank and one from the government. He denied wrongdoing and said he had negotiated a severance package to offset the lower ministerial pay. The accusation was anonymous and no charge, inquiry or ruling is reported, so it stands as an allegation only.
cases.source_title: Former Seychelles governor denies drawing double wage (Central Banking)

cases.people: Venel Joseph (former governor)
cases.summary: Venel Joseph, former governor of the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti, was barred from leaving the country in April 2004 by justice minister Bernard Gousse, who named him among 37 former officials to be kept available for investigations into crimes allegedly committed by the government of ousted president Jean-Bertrand Aristide. The minister described the travel ban as an insurance policy. The source states that he was named in that group as a former official of the Aristide government and does not say what conduct at the central bank, if any, was under investigation, and reports no charge and no finding.
cases.source_title: Ex-cb chief banned from leaving Haiti (Central Banking)

cases.category: conflict of interest in ownership of a commercial bank
cases.people: Central Bank of Armenia, through Housing for Young Families, a refinancing credit organisation it founded
cases.summary: In February 2022 Armbusinessbank's new ownership was registered as MFM Global Invest LLC of Switzerland with 74.998 per cent and Housing for Young Families, a refinancing credit organisation founded by the Central Bank of Armenia, with 25.001 per cent. Former labour minister Maneh Tandilyan publicly called the deal non-transparent and a gross violation of the law barring the regulator from interfering in the activities of commercial banks, and the central bank gave no comment to the news agency. The allegation rests on that one named former official's public statement, no inquiry or ruling is reported, and it stands as a claim rather than a finding.
cases.source_title: 'Mysterious' deal in Armenian banking sector or how Central Bank became shareholder of commercial bank (ArmBanks)

cases.category: audit finding: unreconciled government accounts at the central bank and unreconciled public debt records it manages
cases.people: Central Bank of Belize and Treasury officials (unnamed)
cases.summary: The Auditor General of Belize reported for the 2011/2012 financial year that the Treasury could not show that 25 bank accounts held by the Central Bank of Belize on behalf of the Government of Belize had been reconciled for the audited period. The same report found that the Commonwealth Secretariat public debt recording system managed by the Central Bank of Belize did not reconcile with the Accountant General's financial statements, and that interest payments recorded by the Central Bank differed from the payments recorded in the government's Smart Stream system. No amounts were given for these findings.
cases.source_title: Report of the Auditor General 2011-2012 (Office of the Auditor General, Belize)

cases.category: public accounts committee finding: material differences between central bank balances and government records
cases.people: Maria Rodriguez (Auditor General of Belize); Teresita Miranda (Accountant General of Belize)
cases.summary: The Joint Public Accounts Committee of Belize's National Assembly, reporting on the Auditor General's report for April 2016 to March 2017, listed as a priority area 'Significant material differences between Central Bank and SmartStream balances', with discrepancies totalling 42 million, 19 million, 3 million and 1.4 million dollars. At the Committee's hearings in March 2026 Auditor General Maria Rodriguez said that not even the Central Bank accounts were being reconciled, and referred to differences noted between confirmation letters received from the Central Bank and the government's records. The Committee recorded that the 19,489,652.02 dollar difference shown for the Debt Service Escrow Account was a typographical error with no actual difference, which the Auditor General confirmed.
cases.source_title: Report from the Joint Public Accounts Committee on the Report of the Auditor General for the Year April 2016 to March 2017 (National Assembly of Belize)

cases.people: Accountant General of Barbados (unnamed); Auditor General of Barbados (unnamed)
cases.summary: The Auditor General's 2004 report found discrepancies between the Accountant General's records and the records of the Central Bank of Barbados for the government current account, arising between October 2000 and February 2004. Withdrawals not recorded by the Accountant General exceeded $1.8 million and unrecorded deposits exceeded $6.8 million, including a $4.48 million transaction the Auditor General had already said in 2003 warranted investigation.
cases.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2004 (Barbados Audit Office)

cases.people: Treasury Department / Accountant General staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: The Auditor General's 2020 report found that bank reconciliations for Treasury accounts at the Central Bank of Barbados were not completed up to 31 March 2019, and that the Central Bank account had last been reconciled in May 2018. The report noted that monthly reconciliation is an internal control that can detect fraud or errors.
cases.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2020 (Barbados Audit Office)

cases.category: lending to government beyond legal limits
cases.people: John Rolle (Governor, Central Bank of The Bahamas)
cases.summary: The Bahamian government drew down $232.3 million of IMF special drawing rights held through the Central Bank of The Bahamas in December 2022. The opposition's finance spokesman Kwasi Thompson said the advance was contrary to section 21 of the Central Bank Act, which sets limits on how much the bank may lend or advance to the government, and the government then tabled a bill stating that section 21 would not apply to the transaction and deemed to have come into force on 1 December 2022. Governor John Rolle said in early January that a memorandum of understanding between the bank and the Ministry of Finance stipulated a change to the Central Bank Act.
cases.source_title: Come clean on $232m loan made lawful retroactively (The Tribune, Nassau)
cases.quote: They did in fact have a loan or advance from the Central Bank that was contrary to the law.

cases.summary: A performance audit of government debt servicing carried out by the Samoa Audit Office in 2014 found instances where repayments of government debt had been delayed, comparing due dates with the actual dates the payments were made by the Central Bank of Samoa. The audit also recorded that there was no formalised arrangement between the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank, and its recommendations were directed at the Ministry of Finance, including that the two bodies formalise their responsibilities. No wrongdoing by any person is alleged in the report as described.

cases.quote: The audit team highlighted instances where delays of debts repayments had occurred.

The same page states that earlier in his career he worked for the accounting firms KPMG Peat Marwick, in Saint Lucia, New Zealand and Barbados, and Peat Marwick Mitchell and Co in Saint Lucia, and that he served on the boards of East Caribbean Financial Holding Co. Ltd and Jalousie (1996) Ltd. East Caribbean Financial Holding is a financial holding company. The page gives no dates for any of these roles and does not say whether East Caribbean Financial Holding, Jalousie (1996) Ltd or the accounting firms are privately owned or state-owned, so which side of his career is private is not characterised by this source. The page also records that he chaired the National Insurance Corporation Investment Committee and the Saint Lucia Air and Seaports Authority, both public bodies.

The same page states that after leaving the Central Bank he chaired Commonwealth Bank, a Bahamian commercial bank, as well as the Securities Commission and the College of The Bahamas Council, and served as Ambassador to the United States. The central bank's page gives no dates for the Commonwealth Bank chairmanship beyond placing it after he demitted office in May 1980, and it does not say whether Commonwealth Bank is privately owned or state-owned. revolving_door.people: Abdellatif Jouahri (Wali, i.e. Governor, of Bank Al-Maghrib from 2003; previously president of BMCE until 1995 and then president of the CIMR)
revolving_door.summary: Le Matin's report of 23 April 2003 on King Mohammed VI naming Abdellatif Jouahri wali of Bank Al-Maghrib sets out his career. It states he was president of BMCE, the Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, until 1995, the year the bank was privatised and taken over by Othman Benjelloun, after which he stepped back from business affairs; he was then appointed president of the CIMR, the Caisse Interprofessionnelle Marocaine de Retraites, and reworked it after a major reform; and he was then named wali of the central bank. Bank of Africa's own investor-relations page on its board of directors independently states that Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur was privatised in 1995 and that the sale attracted a consortium of Moroccan and foreign institutional and financial investors led by Royale Marocaine d'Assurance. Neither source states that BMCE was privately owned during Jouahri's presidency, and both place the privatisation at the end of it, so on this evidence the BMCE side of his career was not private. The CIMR side is different. The official summary sheet published by Morocco's insurance and social-welfare regulator ACAPS, at https://acapsd10new.fornetmaroc.com/sites/default/files/fiche_synthetique_cimr.pdf, states that the CIMR was founded by a group of private-sector employers, was managed as an employers' association governed by the dahir of 15 November 1958 on associations, has governing bodies made up only of employer representatives, operates a voluntary scheme supplementary to the state social security system run by the CNSS, and converted into a societe mutuelle de retraite only in 2017 under Law 64-12. So the regulator's own text establishes that the CIMR was a private-sector employers' pension body, not a statutory public pension fund, at the time Jouahri led it immediately before taking the governorship. Le Matin gives no start or end dates for the CIMR presidency, so the commonly cited 2002 to 2003 span is not confirmed by these sources.
revolving_door.source_title: S.M. le Roi nomme M. Abdellatif Jouahri wali de Bank Al-Maghrib (Le Matin)
revolving_door.move: from president of the CIMR, a private-sector employers' pension body per the ACAPS regulator, directly into the governorship of Bank Al-Maghrib in 2003

The Deposit Insurance Corporation is a public deposit-insurance body and the Mongolian Bankers Association is an industry association, not a private firm. This record is therefore flagged as a public move; no private-finance revolving door is evidenced for Mongolia.

revolving_door.move: from the World Bank in Washington into the Bank of Mongolia as Advisor to the Governor in 2000

revolving_door.summary: The Central Bank of Kuwait's own profile page for its Deputy Governor states that Sahar A. Al-Rumaih has been Deputy Governor and a member of the Board of Directors since September 2022, and that almost her whole earlier career was spent in commercial banking. The page says she began in corporate banking and credit at two Kuwaiti banks, then in 2000 joined what it calls 'a large commercial bank in Kuwait', where she was General Manager of the Corporate Credit Division from 2011 to 2018, Head of the Retail Banking Division from 2015 to 2018, and Deputy Chief Executive Officer heading the Corporate and International Banking Divisions from 2018 to 2021. In 2021 she moved to what the page calls 'another major bank headquartered in Kuwait' as Deputy CEO for the Corporate Banking Division. From February 2022 until her appointment as Deputy Governor she was Chairperson of a local capital investment company that the page says is regulated by the Capital Markets Authority. The central bank does not name any of these employers, and names the type only in the one case: the 2000 employer is called a commercial bank. It does not characterise the second bank, nor call the investment company an asset manager or brokerage. The private side of the career is therefore the commercial-banking employment from 2000 to 2021; the public side is the Central Bank of Kuwait. Because the bank gives the career but withholds the employers' names, no firms are listed.
revolving_door.source_title: Deputy Governor (Central Bank of Kuwait)
revolving_door.move: two decades in commercial banking in Kuwait, rising to Deputy CEO, then into the central bank as Deputy Governor

revolving_door.summary: The Central Bank of the Republic of China publishes the curriculum-vitae table for its 21st Board of Directors, appointed for a term running from 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030. In that official table the director 陳思寬 (Chen Szu-kuan) is listed with her current occupation given as Chairman of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited, Chairman of SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited, and adjunct professor at National Taiwan University. This is not a move but a seat held at the same time as the private role: she sits on the central bank's board while chairing a financial holding company and a securities investment trust firm. The central bank's table names the companies and gives her titles but says nothing about ownership, so it does not itself establish that the SinoPac group is private. The trade publication Caproasia, in an article dated 31 March 2026 on a merger of two SinoPac subsidiaries, describes the planned combined bank of Bank SinoPac and King's Town Bank as 'the 5th largest privately-owned bank in Taiwan' and says SinoPac Financial Holdings was founded in 2002 by the Ho family as part of the Yuen Foong Yu Group. Bank SinoPac's own corporate profile confirms it is a wholly owned subsidiary of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited, formed in 2002 through a share swap with Bank SinoPac and SinoPac Securities, but that profile does not state ownership type. So the private characterisation rests on the trade publication, not on the central bank or the group's own page. The central bank side is public.
revolving_door.status: concurrent private and central bank role, no finding

revolving_door.move: from Director General of the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Industry and Tourism, and earlier senior posts at the Vanuatu Chamber of Commerce, Airports Vanuatu Limited, VANAIR and the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, to the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu board
revolving_door.summary: The Reserve Bank's own press release on its 12 September 2014 board appointments says Alilee holds the position of Director General of the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Industry and Tourism, and lists earlier senior executive posts in government ministries and statutory bodies including the Vanuatu Chamber of Commerce, Airports Vanuatu Limited, VANAIR and the Vanuatu National Provident Fund. It gives no dates. Jimmy Nipo was re-appointed in the same release; his background is given as the New Zealand High Commission and Director General of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. No bank, insurer or investment firm is named for either man, so this is filed as a public-sector move.
revolving_door.status: career move, no finding; public-sector move
revolving_door.source_title: Press Release 06 2014: Board Appointments (Reserve Bank of Vanuatu)
revolving_door.quote: He holds the current position of the Director General of the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Industry and Tourism.

revolving_door.people: Nadezhda Yermakova (chaired the National Bank of Belarus 2011-2014)
revolving_door.move: from chair of the National Bank of Belarus (2011-2014) to head of the board of directors of Belgazprombank OJSC (appointed 15 January 2021)
revolving_door.summary: The report says Yermakova chaired the board of Belarusbank and then the National Bank of Belarus in 2011-2014, and was appointed head of Belgazprombank's board of directors on 15 January 2021, having run the bank's interim administration from 15 June to 11 December 2020. Ownership is stated and mixed: the same page names Russian Gazprom PJSC and Gazprombank JSC as holders of 49.66% each, Gazprom Transgaz Belarus 0.49% and the Republic of Belarus, through its Ministry of Energy, 0.097%.
revolving_door.status: career move, no finding; public-sector move

revolving_door.quote: Nadezhda Yermakova was appointed head of the Board of Directors of Belgazprombank OJSC on January 15, 2021

revolving_door.people: Juan Diego Mosquera Pesantes (Banco Central del Ecuador, delegate and member of the Monetary Board, 1981; director and board member of Produbanco since 2014)
revolving_door.move: from Citibank Quito founding manager and Banco del Azuay manager to delegate and member of the Monetary Board at the Banco Central del Ecuador (1981), then to the board of Produbanco (Banco de la Produccion S.A.) from 2014
revolving_door.summary: Produbanco's own curriculum vitae for its board member lists, among his posts, 'Banco Central del Ecuador. Delegado-Vocal de la Junta Monetaria' in 1981, and his service as director and board member of Banco de la Produccion S.A. Produbanco from 2014 onwards. The same CV lists earlier private-bank posts at Citibank Quito, Banco del Pichincha, Banco del Azuay, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and BAC Corp Securities.

revolving_door.people: Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf (Central Bank of Libya from 1985; Director of the Governor's Office 1999-2012 and again from 2024)
revolving_door.move: from Director of the Governor's Office at the Central Bank of Libya (1999-2012) to bank board seats: board member of Arab Italian Bank (UBAE) 2005-2012, member of the Libyan Foreign Bank Supervisory Committee 2007-2012, Deputy Chairman of the Libyan Financial Services Company 2009-2024 and supervisory committee member of Joumhourria Bank 2012-2022
revolving_door.summary: A&T Bank's own board biography gives a full dated career: he began at the Central Bank of Libya's Research Department in 1985, was Director of the Governor's Office there from 1999 to 2012, advised its research and statistics department 2012-2024, and was reappointed Director of the Governor's Office in 2024. Alongside this it lists board or supervisory seats at Arab Italian Bank (UBAE), the Libyan Foreign Bank, the Libyan Financial Services Company and Joumhourria Bank. The page states no ownership for any of those firms, and the Libyan Foreign Bank and Joumhourria Bank are state institutions, so the move is filed as a public-sector move and is not counted.

revolving_door.quote: Director of the Governor's Office at the Central Bank of Libya
